metadata.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
metadata.authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel

nodes.name: Diffusion model (latent variable model)
nodes.statement: A diffusion model is a latent variable model $p_\theta(\bx_0) \defeq \int p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})\, d\bx_{1:T}$, where $\bx_1,\dotsc,\bx_T$ are latents of the same dimensionality as the data $\bx_0 \sim q(\bx_0)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines a diffusion model as a latent variable model where the latents have the same dimensionality as the data and are integrated out.

nodes.name: Reverse process
nodes.statement: The reverse process is the joint $p_\theta(\bx_{0:T}) \defeq p(\bx_T)\prod_{t=1}^T p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)$, a Markov chain with learned Gaussian transitions $p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t) \defeq \mathcal{N}(\bx_{t-1}; \bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t), \bSigma_\theta(\bx_t,t))$, starting at $p(\bx_T)=\mathcal{N}(\bx_T;\bzero,\bI)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reverse process: a Markov chain with learned Gaussian transitions starting from a standard normal prior.

nodes.name: Forward (diffusion) process
nodes.statement: The forward process $q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0) \defeq \prod_{t=1}^T q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})$ is fixed to a Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise: $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1}) \defeq \mathcal{N}(\bx_t;\sqrt{1-\beta_t}\bx_{t-1},\beta_t \bI)$, with variance schedule $\beta_1,\dotsc,\beta_T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fixed Markov chain that progressively adds Gaussian noise according to a variance schedule.

nodes.name: Notation $\alpha_t$ and $\bar\alpha_t$
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha_t \defeq 1-\beta_t$ and $\bar\alpha_t \defeq \prod_{s=1}^t \alpha_s$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines cumulative noise-schedule quantities used throughout.

nodes.name: Discrete decoder $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$
nodes.section: 3.3 Data scaling and reverse process decoder
nodes.statement: An independent discrete decoder derived from $\mathcal{N}(\bx_0;\bmu_\theta(\bx_1,1),\sigma_1^2 \bI)$ assigning to each pixel coordinate the integral of the Gaussian density over a bin of width $\frac{1}{255}$ (with $\pm\infty$ at the edges).
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the final decoder step that produces discrete pixel log-likelihoods by integrating a Gaussian over each $\tfrac{1}{255}$ bin.

nodes.name: Simplified training objective $L_\mathrm{simple}$
nodes.statement: $L_\mathrm{simple}(\theta) \defeq \Eb{t,\bx_0,\bepsilon}{\| \bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon, t) \|^2}$ with $t \sim \mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dotsc,T\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the simplified noise-prediction MSE training loss used in DDPM.

nodes.name: Variational bound on negative log-likelihood
nodes.statement: $\Ea{-\log p_\theta(\bx_0)} \leq \Eb{q}{-\log \frac{p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})}{q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)}} = \mathbb{E}_q\!\big[ -\log p(\bx_T) - \sum_{t \geq 1} \log \frac{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})} \big] \eqqcolon L$.

nodes.name: Closed-form marginal $q(\bx_t|\bx_0)$
nodes.statement: $q(\bx_t|\bx_0) = \mathcal{N}(\bx_t;\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0,(1-\bar\alpha_t)\bI)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The forward process admits a closed-form marginal at any timestep $t$.

nodes.name: Decomposed variational bound (KL form)
nodes.statement: $L = \mathbb{E}_q\!\big[\underbrace{\kl{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}{p(\bx_T)}}_{L_T} + \sum_{t>1} \underbrace{\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}}_{L_{t-1}} \underbrace{- \log p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)}_{L_0}\big]$.

nodes.name: Forward posterior $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)$
nodes.statement: $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0) = \mathcal{N}(\bx_{t-1};\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0),\tilde\beta_t \bI)$, where $\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0) \defeq \frac{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{t-1}}\beta_t}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \frac{\sqrt{\alpha_t}(1-\bar\alpha_{t-1})}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bx_t$ and $\tilde\beta_t \defeq \frac{1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\beta_t$.

nodes.name: $\bmu_\theta$ parameterization via $\bepsilon_\theta$
nodes.statement: $\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t) = \tilde\bmu_t\!\big(\bx_t,\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}}(\bx_t-\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t))\big) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}\!\big(\bx_t - \tfrac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)\big)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The proposed parameterization expressing the reverse mean through a noise-prediction network $\bepsilon_\theta$.

nodes.name: Denoising-score-matching form of $L_{t-1}$
nodes.statement: $L_{t-1} - C = \Eb{\bx_0,\bepsilon}{\frac{\beta_t^2}{2\sigma_t^2 \alpha_t (1-\bar\alpha_t)}\| \bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon, t) \|^2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under the $\bepsilon$-parameterization, $L_{t-1}$ reduces to a weighted noise-prediction MSE resembling denoising score matching.

nodes.name: Alternate variational bound (rate-distortion form)
nodes.statement: $L = \kl{q(\bx_T)}{p(\bx_T)} + \mathbb{E}_q\!\Big[\sum_{t \geq 1} \kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}\Big] + H(\bx_0)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Alternative decomposition of the variational bound used to interpret $L$ as rate plus distortion plus data entropy.

nodes.name: Progressive estimate $\hat\bx_0$
nodes.statement: $\bx_0 \approx \hat\bx_0 = (\bx_t - \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\,\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t))/\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Closed-form estimate of $\bx_0$ from the current noisy iterate $\bx_t$ using the noise predictor.

nodes.name: Training
nodes.statement: Stochastic-gradient training of the noise-prediction network $\bepsilon_\theta$ on the simplified objective $L_\mathrm{simple}$.
nodes.pseudocode: repeat: sample $\bx_0 \sim q(\bx_0)$, $t \sim \mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dotsc,T\}$, $\bepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$; take a gradient step on $\nabla_\theta \| \bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\|^2$; until converged.

nodes.name: Sampling
nodes.statement: Iterative ancestral sampling from the trained reverse process, resembling Langevin dynamics with $\bepsilon_\theta$ as a learned data-density gradient.
nodes.pseudocode: $\bx_T \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$; for $t=T,\dotsc,1$: draw $\bz \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$ if $t>1$ else $\bz=\bzero$; set $\bx_{t-1} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t - \tfrac{1-\alpha_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)) + \sigma_t \bz$; return $\bx_0$.

nodes.name: Sending $\bx_0$ (progressive lossy code)
nodes.statement: Progressive sender that transmits $\bx_T,\dotsc,\bx_0$ in sequence using minimal-random-coding-style transmission, achieving total expected codelength equal to the variational bound.
input: Procedure that transmits $\bx \sim q(\bx)$ using $\sim \kl{q}{p}$ bits
nodes.pseudocode: send $\bx_T \sim q(\bx_T|\bx_0)$ using $p(\bx_T)$; for $t=T-1,\dotsc,1$: send $\bx_t \sim q(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1},\bx_0)$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$; send $\bx_0$ using $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$.

nodes.name: Receiving $\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Progressive receiver that reconstructs $\bx_0$ from the bitstream produced by the sender.
nodes.pseudocode: receive $\bx_T$ using $p(\bx_T)$; for $t=T-1,\dotsc,0$: receive $\bx_t$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$; return $\bx_0$.

nodes.name: Likelihood-based training of diffusion models
nodes.section: 2 Background / 3 Diffusion models and denoising autoencoders
nodes.statement: Train parameters $\theta$ of a diffusion model so that $p_\theta(\bx_0)$ matches the data distribution $q(\bx_0)$, by minimizing the variational bound $L$ on $\Ea{-\log p_\theta(\bx_0)}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fit a diffusion model by minimizing a variational upper bound on the data negative log-likelihood.

nodes.name: Image generation via reverse Markov chain
nodes.statement: Given a trained model $\bepsilon_\theta$ and noise schedule $\{\beta_t\}$, draw a sample $\bx_0 \sim p_\theta(\bx_0)$ by simulating the reverse Markov chain from $\bx_T \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Progressive lossy compression of $\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Encode and transmit $\bx_0$ progressively so that the receiver, at any intermediate step $t$, can produce a reconstruction $\hat\bx_0$ whose distortion decreases as more bits are received, with total expected codelength equal to the variational bound.

nodes.name: Unconditional CIFAR10 sample-quality experiments
nodes.statement: Training the DDPM with $L_\mathrm{simple}$ on unconditional CIFAR10 ($T=1000$, linear $\beta$ schedule from $10^{-4}$ to $0.02$) yields Inception score $9.46$ and FID $3.17$, surpassing most prior unconditional and many class-conditional models.

nodes.name: LSUN $256\times256$ samples (Bedroom, Church, Cat)
nodes.statement: Trained on LSUN $256\times256$ classes the model achieves FID $6.36$ (Bedroom), $7.89$ (Church), $19.75$ (Cat); a larger Bedroom model attains FID $4.90$, comparable to ProgressiveGAN.

nodes.name: Reverse-process parameterization ablation
nodes.section: 4.2 Reverse process parameterization and training objective ablation
nodes.statement: Comparing $\tilde\bmu$- vs $\bepsilon$-prediction and learned vs fixed $\bSigma$: $\bepsilon$-prediction with fixed isotropic $\bSigma$ trained on $L_\mathrm{simple}$ wins (IS $9.46$, FID $3.17$); learning a diagonal $\bSigma_\theta$ destabilises training.

nodes.name: CIFAR10 rate-distortion curve
nodes.statement: Applying Algorithms 3-4 to the trained CIFAR10 model yields a steeply decreasing distortion in the low-rate region; rate $\approx 1.78$ bits/dim and distortion $\approx 1.97$ bits/dim, with RMSE $0.95$ on $[0,255]$ at full rate.

nodes.name: Progressive generation of CIFAR10 samples
nodes.statement: Sampling with Algorithm 2 while plotting $\hat\bx_0$ across timesteps shows large-scale features appearing first and fine details last, mirroring autoregressive coarse-to-fine generation.

nodes.name: CelebA-HQ latent-space interpolation
nodes.statement: Interpolation in the diffusion latent space at $t=500$ yields plausible CelebA-HQ $256\times256$ interpolations that smoothly vary pose, skin tone, hairstyle, expression and background; larger $t$ produces coarser interpolations.

nodes.name: $L_T$ is constant when $\beta_t$ are fixed
nodes.statement: When the forward variances $\beta_t$ are held fixed (no learnable parameters in $q$), the term $L_T$ in the decomposed bound is constant during training and can be ignored.

nodes.name: Choices of $\sigma_t^2$ are upper/lower entropy bounds
nodes.statement: Setting $\sigma_t^2 = \beta_t$ is optimal for $\bx_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$ and $\sigma_t^2 = \tilde\beta_t = \frac{1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\beta_t$ is optimal for deterministic $\bx_0$; experimentally both perform similarly.

nodes.name: Connection to autoregressive decoding
nodes.statement: If $T$ equals data dimension and $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})$ masks out the $t$-th coordinate, then training $p_\theta$ recovers an autoregressive model; Gaussian diffusion is therefore a generalised-bit-ordering autoregressive model.

nodes.name: Equivalence with denoising score matching + Langevin dynamics
nodes.statement: Under the $\bepsilon$-parameterization, optimising the diffusion variational bound is equivalent to performing denoising score matching across multiple noise levels and yields a sampler resembling annealed Langevin dynamics.

nodes.name: Variational bound on log-likelihood (Jensen)
nodes.statement: For any latent-variable model $p_\theta(\bx_0,\bx_{1:T})$ and any forward distribution $q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)$: $\Ea{-\log p_\theta(\bx_0)} \leq \Eb{q}{-\log \frac{p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})}{q(\bx_{1:T}|\bx_0)}}$.
assumptions: $p_\theta(\bx_{0:T})$ is a joint density over $\bx_0$ and latents $\bx_{1:T}$
nodes.origin_citation: Jensen's inequality / variational inference; cf. Kingma & Welling 2013

nodes.name: Rao-Blackwellised KL between Gaussians
nodes.statement: Each $L_{t-1} = \kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}$ has a closed-form expression because both arguments are Gaussian, so it can be evaluated without high-variance Monte Carlo estimation.
conclusions: $L_{t-1}$ has a closed-form (Rao-Blackwellised) expression in terms of means and covariances
nodes.origin_citation: Standard fact about Gaussian KL divergence

nodes.name: Derivation of decomposed variational bound
nodes.statement: Manipulate the basic ELBO $L$ by separating the $t=1$ term, applying Bayes' rule $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1}) = q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0) q(\bx_t|\bx_0)/q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_0)$, and telescoping to obtain the KL decomposition $L = L_T + \sum_{t>1} L_{t-1} + L_0$.

nodes.name: Reduction of $L_{t-1}$ to noise-prediction MSE
nodes.statement: Starting from $L_{t-1} = \Eb{q}{\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\|\tilde\bmu_t - \bmu_\theta\|^2}+C$, reparameterise $\bx_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon$, substitute the $\bepsilon$-parameterization of $\bmu_\theta$, and simplify to the weighted MSE in $\bepsilon$.

nodes.name: Derivation of alternate variational bound
nodes.statement: Using $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1}) = q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)q(\bx_t)/q(\bx_{t-1})$ in the basic ELBO and telescoping yields $L = \kl{q(\bx_T)}{p(\bx_T)} + \Eb{q}{\sum_{t \geq 1}\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}} + H(\bx_0)$.

nodes.name: Expand $L$ as expected log-ratio
nodes.statement: Write $L = \Eb{q}{-\log p(\bx_T) - \sum_{t \geq 1}\log \frac{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})}}$.

nodes.name: Split off $t=1$ term
nodes.statement: Separate the sum into $t>1$ and $t=1$ to isolate $-\log \frac{p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)}{q(\bx_1|\bx_0)}$.

nodes.name: Apply Bayes' rule on forward transitions
nodes.statement: Replace $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})$ by $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0) q(\bx_t|\bx_0)/q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_0)$ inside the $t>1$ terms.

nodes.name: Telescope $q(\bx_t|\bx_0)/q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_0)$
nodes.statement: The product over $t$ of these ratios telescopes, leaving $q(\bx_T|\bx_0)/q(\bx_1|\bx_0)$ which combines with the $t=1$ term and $-\log p(\bx_T)$.

nodes.name: Recognise KL divergences
nodes.statement: Identify $\Eb{q}{-\log \frac{p(\bx_T)}{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}}$ as $\kl{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}{p(\bx_T)} = L_T$ and each $\Eb{q}{-\log \frac{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)}}$ as $L_{t-1}$, with $L_0 = -\log p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$.

nodes.name: Start from Gaussian KL form
nodes.statement: Since both $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t,\bx_0)$ and $p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)$ are Gaussian with the same fixed variance $\sigma_t^2 \bI$, $L_{t-1} = \Eb{q}{\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\|\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0)-\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t)\|^2} + C$.

nodes.name: Reparameterise $\bx_t$ via $\bepsilon$
nodes.statement: Use $\bx_t = \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon$ with $\bepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$ from EP12.2 to express $\bx_0$ in terms of $\bx_t$ and $\bepsilon$.

nodes.name: Substitute into $\tilde\bmu_t$
nodes.statement: Plug the reparameterisation into $\tilde\bmu_t(\bx_t,\bx_0)$ and simplify to obtain $\tilde\bmu_t = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t - \tfrac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon)$.

nodes.name: Choose $\bepsilon$-parameterization for $\bmu_\theta$
nodes.statement: Set $\bmu_\theta(\bx_t,t) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}(\bx_t - \tfrac{\beta_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t))$ so that the squared error reduces to $\| \bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)\|^2$ scaled by $\beta_t^2/(2\sigma_t^2 \alpha_t (1-\bar\alpha_t))$.

nodes.name: Conclude denoising-score-matching form
nodes.statement: Collecting terms yields $L_{t-1}-C = \Eb{\bx_0,\bepsilon}{\frac{\beta_t^2}{2\sigma_t^2 \alpha_t (1-\bar\alpha_t)}\|\bepsilon-\bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\|^2}$.

nodes.name: Apply Bayes' rule (unconditional form)
nodes.statement: Replace $q(\bx_t|\bx_{t-1})$ in the ELBO by $q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)q(\bx_t)/q(\bx_{t-1})$ (no conditioning on $\bx_0$).

nodes.name: Telescope $q(\bx_t)/q(\bx_{t-1})$
nodes.statement: The telescoping product yields $q(\bx_T)/q(\bx_0)$, contributing $\kl{q(\bx_T)}{p(\bx_T)}$ and $-\log q(\bx_0)$ to $L$.

nodes.name: Identify entropy and KL terms
nodes.statement: Recognise $-\Eb{q}{\log q(\bx_0)} = H(\bx_0)$ and the per-$t$ residuals as $\kl{q(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}{p_\theta(\bx_{t-1}|\bx_t)}$, giving the alternate bound.

nodes.name: Sample data point
nodes.statement: $\bx_0 \sim q(\bx_0)$.

nodes.name: Sample timestep and noise
nodes.statement: $t \sim \mathrm{Uniform}\{1,\dotsc,T\}$ and $\bepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Take gradient step on $L_\mathrm{simple}$
nodes.statement: Update $\theta$ along $\nabla_\theta \| \bepsilon - \bepsilon_\theta(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}\bx_0 + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\bepsilon,t)\|^2$.

nodes.name: Repeat until converged
nodes.statement: Loop the sample-and-update steps until convergence of the training loss.

nodes.name: Initialise $\bx_T$ from prior
nodes.statement: $\bx_T \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$.

nodes.name: Loop $t = T,\dotsc,1$ with one Langevin-like update
nodes.statement: For $t=T,\dotsc,1$: draw $\bz \sim \mathcal{N}(\bzero,\bI)$ if $t>1$ else $\bz = \bzero$, then set $\bx_{t-1} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{\alpha_t}}\!\big(\bx_t - \tfrac{1-\alpha_t}{\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}}\bepsilon_\theta(\bx_t,t)\big) + \sigma_t \bz$.

nodes.name: Return $\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Return the final $\bx_0$ as the generated sample.

nodes.name: Send $\bx_T$ using prior
nodes.statement: Sample $\bx_T \sim q(\bx_T|\bx_0)$ and transmit it using the prior $p(\bx_T)$ via minimal random coding ($\sim \kl{q(\bx_T|\bx_0)}{p(\bx_T)}$ bits).

nodes.name: Send each $\bx_t$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$
nodes.statement: For $t=T-1,\dotsc,1$: sample $\bx_t \sim q(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1},\bx_0)$ and transmit it using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$.

nodes.name: Send $\bx_0$ using decoder
nodes.statement: Transmit $\bx_0$ using $p_\theta(\bx_0|\bx_1)$.

nodes.name: Receive $\bx_T$
nodes.statement: Receive $\bx_T$ using $p(\bx_T)$.

nodes.name: Receive each $\bx_t$
nodes.statement: For $t=T-1,\dotsc,0$: receive $\bx_t$ using $p_\theta(\bx_t|\bx_{t+1})$.

nodes.name: Return $\bx_0$
nodes.statement: Return the reconstructed $\bx_0$.
